findings.claim: NIX_CACHE_HOME is recognized by Nix itself and, when present, is returned verbatim before consulting XDG_CACHE_HOME. On Unix the fallback is XDG_CACHE_HOME/nix, then HOME/.cache/nix.
The default narinfo SQLite database is getCacheDir()/binary-cache-v7.sqlite.
A missing path has a timestamped present=0 disk row keyed by cache and path hash; negative entries default to a 3600-second TTL. A fresh entry is returned as invalid without querying the server.
After uploading narinfo, the uploader updates its own in-memory entry and selected disk database using its local narinfo object. It does not fetch server-modified metadata in this function.

An actually separate temporary uploader cache prevents its locally generated metadata from replacing normal consumer cache records, but also leaves pre-existing consumer negative entries untouched. This follows from the selected database and process-local memory update paths.
When an uploader and consumer share a database, upload can replace the negative disk row, but a different live process can still return a fresh negative memory entry before consulting disk.

A hook that changes only XDG_CACHE_HOME does not isolate the narinfo database if NIX_CACHE_HOME is inherited. A temporary NIX_CACHE_HOME override, or unsetting it within the hook before using temporary XDG_CACHE_HOME, would address directory selection. No such change was applied.
